name: Margin Tutoring
tagline: Tutoring that shows up on the report card.
area: Harrow Hill, Eastbrook and online anywhere

assessment.title: Forty minutes, one subject
assessment.body: With the tutor who would teach your child, in person or online.

assessment.title: Bring the last report card
assessment.body: And a recent test or piece of homework, marked or not.

assessment.title: A written summary in two days
assessment.body: What we found, where the gap is, and the plan we would suggest.

assessment.title: No obligation
assessment.body: Most families book, some do not. Either way the summary is yours.

art_direction.identity: Exercise-book paper, blue-black ink and one red pen. Fraunces set like a well-made school book over DM Sans text, faint ruled lines, a red margin rule, and Caveat only for the short red-pen notes a teacher writes in the margin.
art_direction.type: Fraunces 400–500 with the soft axis at 50 for every heading, never bold; DM Sans at 1.0625rem/1.7 for body. Caveat is reserved for two- to six-word margin notes in the accent colour.
art_direction.color: Paper (bg-canvas) is roughly three quarters of any viewport. Red pen (accent) marks — the primary button, the margin rule, circled grades and hand notes — and never fills a field. Blue-black (bg-deep) belongs to the closing band and the footer only. The pale ruled blue (bg-panel) holds the report card. No gradients, no third brand colour.
art_direction.signature: The report card — a typeset term report of real students (shared with permission), the grade they started on and the grade they reached, the new grade circled in red pen and a handwritten note in the margin. Keep it wherever the design evolves.
art_direction.voice: A good teacher's report: plain, specific and warm. Name the subject, the year group and the weeks it took. Two sentences maximum, no exclamation points, never 'unlock your potential'.
